claims.text: Replacing an EAM reference with an MLIP trained on broadly sampled ab initio liquid configurations will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch in high-entropy alloys near melting.
The proposed method is intended for multicomponent high-entropy alloys in both solid and liquid states near their melting temperatures.
A neural-network or moment-tensor MLIP with many-body descriptors should be used as the thermodynamic-integration reference instead of a conventional EAM model.
The proposed applicability range comprises alloys with at least five principal elements.
The proposed temperature range is approximately 0.9–1.1 times the melting temperature.
An appropriately trained MLIP can capture the complex many-body interactions and diverse local atomic configurations of multicomponent-alloy liquids.
Training on a wide variety of ab initio liquid configurations makes the MLIP reproduce the relevant potential-energy surface more accurately.
More accurate reproduction of the potential-energy surface improves reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved phase-space overlap reduces thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to EAM-based TOR-TILD.
The MLIP reference is predicted to improve thermodynamic-integration mismatch by approximately 50–70% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
MLIP-based free-energy calculations are predicted to agree more closely with direct ab initio estimates than EAM-reference calculations do.
TOR-TILD EAM references inadequately represent the configurational diversity of the liquid.
The approach may cease to be reliable for chemical disorder outside typical high-entropy-alloy compositions if such configurations are absent from training.
The approach may cease to be reliable at temperatures substantially outside the melting regime if the training data are not representative there.
The quantitative reduction in mismatch depends on training-set quality and representativeness, descriptors, and model architecture.
A reduction of less than 50% in path mismatch relative to the EAM reference is specified as a falsifying result.
